Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you turn this into a usable request for a community survey export, i have the workbook called Northbank Access Check and it will be attached with the request. the survey was about getting around the Northbank area and using the neighborhood library, and it was open March 3 through March 17, 2025. the workbook has a Responses tab, a Codebook tab, and a Delivery tab. the Responses tab has 186 records according to the sheet, and nine have the status Practice, those are trial submissions from staff, not community responses. i need one row per remaining submitted response and don't combine people or calculate a summary in place of the rows. The point is a handoff file that someone can open without having to figure out which columns mean what.

I need a comma-delimited CSV and a short readme beside it. Use UTF-8, keep the row-level data, and use the Codebook for meanings of coded answers. Don't try to write up what residents think or draw conclusions about the survey. The comment answers matter because they are people's own words. the coordinator told me, “keep the comment text as people wrote it.” So leave spelling, punctuation, and line breaks within an answer alone as far as CSV allows, and quote or escape commas, quotes, and line breaks correctly so a comment doesn't spill into another column or record. Don't tidy comments, remove names from them, or make them sound more consistent. No need to translate anything. Keep blanks blank rather than putting in a guess like none or not applicable.

There are a few field details i want clear in the prompt, because we have had confusion about this before. Include Response ID as the first column and keep it as a text value, even if some IDs look numeric. The Response Date comes next. After those, include the four survey question fields in the order they appear in the Responses tab, then the optional comment field, then Ward. Use the field labels from the Codebook for the question fields, not shortened labels. The source column names for those questions are Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4. The exact question wording is in the Codebook. The Ward field should be last, since that makes it easier for the library staff to compare their local notes. Include the fields in this order even if they're blank for a response; don't drop a column because nobody filled it in. For dates just keep the date that is in the workbook, don't convert them into something inferred from the survey dates or change a date based on when somebody submitted.

For which rows: exclude rows whose status is exactly Practice. don't remove other rows based on a guess, and don't treat a blank answer as a reason to drop a response. If a response has one or more blank survey answers it still gets its row. Keep one record per included response and don't sort by the comment or answer values. Keep the order of included records as in the Responses tab. The Delivery tab has the recipient information and a short note about the handoff. Address the export to Bram, not Saskia. Please use the name exactly that way in the readme and don't add anyone else as a recipient. There is a note in Delivery that the library team receives the file but it doesn't list a different person, so don't turn the team into an extra named recipient.

The Codebook has descriptions for Q1 through Q4 and says which answers use codes. Include the readable answer label for coded answers in the CSV, rather than just leaving a numeric code that a reader has to decode, but retain the original values for answers that are not coded. If a code in a response doesn't match the Codebook, don't choose the closest label or repair it; leave that value as it is and mention the unmatched code in the readme without naming a respondent. The Codebook's description for Ward is just that it is the Northbank ward where a respondent lives, so don't derive ward from a comment or from any other answer. If the Ward cell is blank, leave it blank. The workbook doesn't state a preferred filename, so give the CSV a plain descriptive filename based on the survey title and the readme should have a matching base name.

In the readme, explain what workbook and sheet the export came from, that Practice rows were excluded, what the columns represent, that coded answers were rendered using the Codebook, and who the file is for. Keep this short and useful, not a report on the survey. There is no need to list people's comments or reproduce any respondent-level data in the readme. If you encounter a workbook issue that affects the requested export, state the issue instead of silently making a choice. Don't invent missing values, labels, or facts, and don't claim a check was done if it wasn't possible from the attached workbook.

The survey covered getting around the Northbank area and using the neighborhood library, and was open from March 3 through March 17, 2025. The workbook contains a Responses tab, a Codebook tab, and a Delivery tab. The Responses tab lists 186 records, including nine staff trial submissions whose status is Practice.

## Deliverables and recipient

Create one comma-delimited, UTF-8 CSV containing one row per submitted response, excluding rows whose status is exactly Practice, and a short readme beside it. Address the export to **Bram, not Saskia**. Use that name exactly in the readme, and do not add another named recipient. The Delivery tab says the library team receives the file but does not identify a different person; do not turn the team into an additional named recipient.

Use a plain descriptive filename based on the survey title for the CSV, and give the readme the same base name. The handoff is due Friday, March 21, 2025, by 3 p.m. local time.

## CSV contents

Keep one row per included response. Do not combine records, calculate a summary instead of providing rows, or drop a response because an answer is blank. Do not apply any additional row filters based on guesses. Keep the included records in their original order from the Responses tab, and do not sort by comments or answer values.

Use these columns in this order:

1. Response ID, as a text value even when an ID looks numeric.
2. Response Date.
3. The four survey question fields in the order they appear in the Responses tab, using the full field labels from the Codebook rather than shortened labels. Their source column names are Q1, Q2, Q3, and Q4; the Codebook contains the exact question wording.
4. The optional comment field.
5. Ward, as the final column.

Include every specified column even if it is blank for a response. Preserve the date shown in the workbook; do not infer or change dates based on the survey period or submission timing. Leave blank cells blank rather than substituting values such as “none” or “not applicable.”

Use the Codebook to interpret coded answers. For coded answers, include the readable answer label in the CSV. For answers that are not coded, retain their original values. If a response contains a code that does not match the Codebook, leave the value as it is; do not select a similar label or repair it. Mention any unmatched code in the readme without identifying a respondent.

The Codebook describes Ward as the Northbank ward where the respondent lives. Do not infer Ward from a comment or another answer, and leave a blank Ward cell blank.

## Comments and file handling

Keep comment text in the respondents’ own words. As the coordinator put it, “keep the comment text as people wrote it.” Do not edit spelling or punctuation, tidy or standardize comments, remove names, or translate them. Preserve line breaks within an answer as far as CSV allows. Quote or escape commas, quotation marks, and line breaks correctly so each comment remains in its proper field and record.

Do not write an account of what residents think or draw conclusions from the survey. The export is for row-level handoff, not analysis, charts, interpretation, or a rewritten version of the comments.

## Readme and workbook issues

Keep the readme short and practical. State which workbook and sheet the export came from, that Practice rows were excluded, what the columns represent, that coded answers were rendered using the Codebook, and who the file is for. Do not reproduce comments or other respondent-level data in it.

If an issue with the workbook affects a requested step, identify the specific issue rather than silently choosing a solution. Do not invent missing values, labels, or facts, and do not claim a check was completed if the attached workbook did not allow it. You may state that no issue was found only if you checked the workbook."}]
